account:
It is late morning on day 1. I have completed a limited grain inspection at the mill: its stall chest contains 128 hay bales, priced at two emeralds each. I have not checked their quality or established the town's full supply. My next scheduled obligations are lunch at home at noon and council letters in the office at one.

The unusual matter is a persistent, vague story about a bridge or port change at the bakery. Several townsfolk near the mill repeat almost identical words, but none has explained an actual proposal or change. Townsfolk 11 associates the report with the baker, Freight and Neighbour being at the bakery, and says the baker carried a sack of bread. That bread carrying could simply be normal business; I have no evidence that it means anything secret. I also heard the baker shouting earlier, but could not understand the words.

Yesterday the innkeeper denied proposing or announcing a change and traced the vague rumor to Townsfolk 03. Builder reported the bridge passable without confirmed defects, and relayed Freight's account of sound roads and an uneventful ferry crossing. These reports do not establish any need for repairs. Today I authorized Builder only to conduct a two-emerald visual survey, payable on delivery of written findings, with no repairs or alterations permitted. Separate one-emerald book expenses for Builder and Secretary have been supplied and recorded. Secretary retains my original appointment book and says there is still no verified news of a bridge or port change.

I suspect a discussion concerning transport or supplies may be spreading as rumor, but I do not yet know its purpose or whether there is any real plan behind it. I should ask the baker directly what was said, who proposed it, and what, if anything, is intended to change, without presenting rumor as fact. Secretary is helping preserve records and appointments; Neighbour was asked to pass an invitation to Townsfolk 03, whose attendance remains unconfirmed.
